column2: The class nominated Emma as their representative for the school council.
column3: 全班提名艾瑪擔任學生議會的班級代表。
column5: nomin 名字：把某人的名字提出來，就是提名

column2: The guide oriented the new students by showing them where every classroom was.
column3: 導覽員帶新生認識每間教室的位置，讓他們熟悉環境。
column4: orient new students (讓新生熟悉環境)
column5: orient 本義是東方（日出方向）；用來定方向，就找到位置

column2: They ornamented the hall with paper lanterns and green leaves.
column3: 他們用紙燈籠和綠葉裝飾禮堂。
column5: ornament 是裝飾品；動詞就是掛上裝飾品

column2: Our team trained hard to outdo last year's champions.
column3: 我們的隊伍努力訓練，要勝過去年的冠軍。
column5: out 超出 + do 做：比別人做得更多更好

column2: Don't overdo the exercise on your first day back at the gym.
column3: 重回健身房的第一天不要運動過頭。
column5: over 過度 + do 做：做得太超過

column2: We always overeat at the New Year dinner and feel sleepy afterward.
column3: 我們每次吃新年團圓飯都吃得過飽，之後昏昏欲睡。
column5: over 過度 + eat 吃：吃過頭，肚子撐

column2: Heavy rain made the river overflow, and water covered the nearby road.
column3: 大雨讓河水滿溢，淹沒了附近的道路。
column5: over 越過 + flow 流：水流出了邊界

column2: I accidentally overheard my sister planning a surprise party for Mom.
column3: 我無意中聽到姊姊正在籌劃給媽媽的驚喜派對。
column4: overhear a conversation (無意聽到談話)
column5: over 越過 + hear 聽：話飄過來剛好被聽到

column2: I overslept this morning and missed the first bus to school.
column3: 我今天早上睡過頭，錯過了去學校的第一班公車。
column4: oversleep and miss class (睡過頭而錯過上課)
column5: over 過頭 + sleep 睡：睡得超過鬧鐘時間

column2: The crowd's cheering overwhelmed the shy singer, and she forgot her lines.
column3: 群眾的歡呼聲讓害羞的歌手招架不住，忘了歌詞。
column5: over 越過 + whelm 淹沒：像大浪蓋過頭頂

column2: The manager overworks his staff, and many of them are very tired.
column3: 那位經理讓員工工作過度，許多人都累壞了。
column5: over 過度 + work 工作：工作到超過負荷

column2: We paddled the canoe slowly across the calm lake.
column3: 我們划著獨木舟，緩緩划過平靜的湖面。
column5: paddle 像「拍斗」：拿船槳拍水往前走

column2: Security guards patrol the school grounds every night.
column3: 警衛每晚都在校園裡巡邏。
column5: patrol 像「怕脫」：有人巡邏，壞人就怕得脫身

column2: The hen pecked at the corn scattered across the yard.
column3: 母雞啄著撒在院子裡的玉米粒。
column5: peck 像「佩克」：雞嘴一下一下啄，像在說「配克」

column2: The little boy peeked through the keyhole to see his birthday gift.
column3: 小男孩從鑰匙孔偷看他的生日禮物。
column4: peek through a hole (從洞中偷看)
column5: peek 像「皮克」：從門縫露出一點，偷偷瞧一眼

column2: Campers pegged the tent firmly to the ground before the storm arrived.
column3: 露營的人在暴風雨來臨前，用木釘把帳篷牢牢釘在地上。
column4: peg a tent down (用釘子固定帳篷)
column5: peg 是釘子；動詞就是把東西釘住

column2: Several sparrows perched on the wire and chirped in the morning light.
column3: 幾隻麻雀停在電線上，在晨光中嘰嘰喳喳叫著。
column4: birds perch on a branch (鳥停在樹枝上)
column5: perch 像「拍曲」：鳥停下來拍拍翅膀休息

column2: Reckless driving can peril everyone on the road.
column3: 魯莽駕駛會危及路上的每一個人。
column5: peril 是危險；動詞就是把人放進危險裡

column2: She persisted in practicing the violin even when her fingers hurt.
column3: 即使手指痛，她仍堅持練小提琴。
column5: per 徹底 + sist 站住：站穩不放棄，就是堅持

column2: The crab pinched my finger when I picked it up from the sand.
column3: 我從沙地撿起螃蟹時，牠夾了我的手指。
column5: pinch 像「拼取」：兩根手指拼在一起就是擰

column2: The scout leader told the boy not to piss near the campsite water.
column3: 童軍團長叫那個男孩不要在營地水源附近小便。
column4: piss in the bushes (在灌木叢小便)
column5: piss 是不太禮貌的粗話，上課和生活常用 pee 較好

column2: In the old film, the cowboy pistoled the lock off the barn door.
column3: 在那部老電影裡，牛仔用手槍把穀倉門上的鎖打掉。
column4: pistol a lock (用手槍射擊鎖)
column5: pistol 是手槍；動詞很少見，指用手槍射出去

column2: The lawyer pleaded the case before a full courtroom.
column3: 律師在擠滿人的法庭上為這件案子辯護。
column5: plead 像「普利」：請求普普利利，求法官答應

column2: The mayor pledged to build a new library by next summer.
column3: 市長承諾明年夏天以前蓋好一座新圖書館。
column5: pledge 像「普列奇」：舉手發誓，保證給予

column2: Farmers plowed the wet fields before planting rice in spring.
column3: 農夫們在春天插秧之前先犁過濕潤的田地。
column5: plow 像「泡」：牛拉著犁，把田裡土壤翻起來

column2: She plucked a few ripe berries from the bush and ate them.
column3: 她從灌木叢上摘下幾顆熟透的莓果來吃。
column5: pluck 像「普拉克」：用手指啪地一下摘下來

column2: The diver plunged into the lake and swam toward the bottom.
column3: 潛水者跳入湖中，往湖底游去。
column5: plunge 像「潘吉」：噗通一聲跳進水裡

column2: He poked the campfire with a stick to make it burn brighter.
column3: 他用樹枝撥弄營火，讓火燒得更旺。
column5: poke 像「破客」：用手指或棍子戳一戳

column2: The priest preached about kindness to a quiet hall of listeners.
column3: 牧師對著安靜的聽眾講道，內容是關於善良。
column5: preach 像「皮區」：牧師的嘴一直說教

column2: Despite the storm, justice prevailed and the team won the final match.
column3: 儘管遇上暴風雨，球隊仍然取勝，贏得決賽。
column4: truth will prevail (真理終將勝出)
column5: pre 先 + vail 強：實力最強的最後勝出

column2: The studio will preview the new film for critics on Friday.
column3: 片廠將在星期五為影評人試映這部新電影。
column5: pre 先 + view 看：先看一遍

column2: The thorn pricked her finger, and a tiny drop of blood appeared.
column3: 刺扎到她的手指，冒出一小滴血。
column5: prick 像「普力克」：被針尖「普」地刺一下

column2: The magazine profiled a local chef who cooks for the elderly.
column3: 雜誌為一位替老人煮飯的在地主廚寫了人物簡介。
column4: profile a chef (為主廚寫人物簡介)
column5: profile 是側臉輪廓；動詞就是描出一個人的輪廓

column2: Bad weather prolonged our trip by two days.
column3: 惡劣的天氣使我們的旅程延長了兩天。
column5: pro 向前 + long 長：往前拉長

column2: He propped the door open with a heavy book.
column3: 他用一本厚重的書把門撐開。
column4: prop a door open (把門撐開)
column5: prop 像「撲」：用東西撐住讓它不倒

column2: The architect proportioned the rooms so that each had enough light.
column3: 建築師按比例設計各個房間，使每間都有足夠的光線。
column4: proportion the rooms (使房間比例協調)
column5: pro 向 + portion 一份：分得剛好，比例才對

column2: Early settlers prospected for gold in the rivers of the western hills.
column3: 早期移民在西部山區的河流裡尋找金礦。
column5: pro 往前 + spect 看：往前看土裡有沒有礦

column2: Dad prunes the apple trees every winter so they grow better.
column3: 爸爸每年冬天都修剪蘋果樹，讓它們長得更好。
column5: prune 也是李子乾；修掉多餘的枝，樹才健康

column2: The old train puffed up the hill, sending white smoke into the sky.
column3: 老火車噗噗地爬上山坡，把白煙吐向天空。
column5: puff 的聲音就像「噗」：一陣一陣地吹氣

column2: His heart pulsed fast as he waited for the exam results.
column3: 等待考試成績時，他的心臟怦怦快速跳動。
column5: pulse 像「怕死」：心臟怦怦跳，嚇得脈搏加速
